source.title: Residual Koopman Spectral Profiling for Predicting and Preventing Transformer Training Instability
source.authors: Bum Jun Kim; Shohei Taniguchi; M. Kawano; Yusuke Iwasawa; Yutaka Matsuo

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures and reduces training divergence, but does not measure training classification error or test any of the listed versions about training error, shortcuts, initialization, learning-rate recovery, or batch-normalization speed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports divergence rates, validation accuracy, and perplexity for its own RKSP/KSS stability experiments. These do not establish whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero. The paper's discussion of Fixup and ReZero is textual; it reports no new training result for those methods.
record.test_reason: The study measures transformer divergence, spectral diagnostics, and validation performance. It does not test any specified version: there are no training-error measurements for the named convolutional networks, teacher–student minima, shortcut or activation-matched initialization comparisons, learning-rate dynamics relative to an initial optimization stability threshold, or batch-normalization comparisons. Layer-transition Koopman spectra are not loss curvature or the stability threshold in V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that RKSP predicts divergence from initialization-time residual spectra and that KSS reduces divergence and permits larger learning rates. They qualify the mechanism with non-normality, linear-fit reliability, and degenerate identity-initialization caveats. AUROC 0.995 describes discrimination; Appendix H reports only moderate probability calibration, with ECE 0.283. Pretrained models up to 7B receive forward-only profiling, not KSS training validation.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes residual Koopman spectral profiling and spectral regularization to predict and prevent training divergence; it does not reproduce the claim's training-error measurements or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported divergence and accuracy vary with normalization strategy and KSS weight; KSS outcomes also vary by model size and architecture. These are stability results, not measurements of the claim's training-error behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalization choices affect transformer divergence and validation accuracy; KSS reduces divergence and improves validation metrics in associative recall, language modeling, and ViT experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral regularization can reduce training divergence and improve validation performance in the tested transformer settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization-time near-unit spectral mass predicts divergence with AUROC 0.995; Table 5 reports higher maximum stable learning rates with KSS. Neither result measures optimization curvature or recovery above its stability threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream spectral diagnostics predict transformer divergence, and KSS increases empirical learning-rate tolerance.

record.problems: The paper reports accuracy and divergence but not training classification error, so its results cannot determine whether networks reach zero or near-zero training error. Several accuracy results are based on few converged runs; the paper explicitly says Table 1 accuracy is computed from only 3 converged runs out of 84. The KSS comparisons report trial counts but no uncertainty intervals for divergence rates or accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the selected related divergence and validation-metric rows.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher–student spurious minima and the effect of additional student neurons.
All parts: depth-dependent training error in plain versus identity-shortcut convolutional networks, very deep plain tanh training, and Fixup training.

All parts: activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. The µP comparison reports transformer stability and validation accuracy, not these outcomes.
All parts: recovery above the initial linearized optimization stability limit, accompanying loss-curvature dynamics, full-batch edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence from below that threshold.

All parts: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training. Layer normalization and RMSNorm comparisons do not test batch normalization.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. The study's divergence label is triggered by loss exceeding 50 or gradient norm exceeding 500 at any step; it does not establish persistent divergence, training-error convergence, or stability relative to a Hessian-derived threshold. Additional method comparisons and profiling results are outside the listed versions, so they do not require entries in missing.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-dependent training error with and without identity shortcuts, and the stated plain-network initialization and normalization-free residual results.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Training above the initial linearized stability limit, loss-curvature dynamics, sharpness at the stability threshold, and the stated divergence cases.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual-network training without normalization.
